editorNote: This week the keyboard becomes a workshop: game makers explain how rules, maps, prose, and player imagination turn modest home computers into whole worlds.
morningLine: Tuesday, May 24, 1983: game design reaches the science pages while shoppers compare disks, joysticks, and the new IBM PC XT.

lead.headline: Game Makers Map the Imaginative Path
lead.dek: Designers turn tiny memories into puzzles, adventures, and worlds the player helps complete.
lead.body: A May 24 New York Times personal-computing column puts game design in the spotlight. The craft is less a matter of spectacle than of carefully chosen rules, feedback, surprise, and room for the player’s imagination. Across the month’s computer magazines, the same inventive energy appears in adventure contests, modem play, construction sets, and reviews of strategy simulations—proof that the home computer is becoming a medium, not merely a machine.
lead.confidence: Exact-day article verified; surrounding game-design context is corroborated by May–June 1983 period magazines.
